steps.title: Apply online for your study permit (visa issued with approval)
steps.why: Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study at a designated learning institution in Canada, and you should apply before you travel. Because your citizenship requires a visitor visa to enter Canada, the temporary resident visa is issued together with your study permit approval — you don't need to apply separately or pay another fee, but the visa is printed in your passport, so plan for the extra time it takes IRCC to return your passport before you book flights. Processing times vary by country, so apply as early as possible after accepting your UBC offer.
prerequisites: Accepted your UBC offer of admission and have your letter of acceptance from UBC (a designated learning institution)
An IRCC secure account to pay fees, submit your application, and check status
A scanner or camera to create electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card
Your visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from
A valid passport — you must travel with the same passport you used to apply, since the visa will be placed in it
steps.cost: CAN $150 study permit fee (no separate fee for the temporary resident visa)
steps.time_estimate: Processing times vary by country; allow extra time for your passport to be submitted and returned with the visa

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics (fingerprints and photo) within 30 days
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics for most study permit applications to confirm your identity and help assess your application. After you submit, IRCC sends a biometric instruction letter — you have 30 days to give your fingerprints and photo, and booking your collection appointment as soon as you can avoids processing delays. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted study permit application online (with letter of acceptance and PAL/TAL)
Paid the biometrics fee at the time you submitted your application
Received the biometric instruction letter from IRCC telling you to give biometrics
steps.cost: CAN$85 per applicant; maximum CAN$170 for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Book immediately on receiving the letter — you have 30 days to give biometrics

steps.title: Book and complete your immigration medical exam with an IRCC panel physician
steps.why: To enter Canada on a study permit you must be in good health, and only a physician authorized by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) can perform an immigration medical exam (IME). Results go directly to the office processing your application, so completing the exam early keeps your study permit application moving and avoids delays before your travel date.
prerequisites: Check your local visa office instructions (selected by country/territory on the IRCC study permit application page) to confirm whether a medical exam is required for you
Know where your study permit application is being processed, so you can tell the physician which office should receive your results
Valid passport or travel document to present at the appointment
Use the IRCC list of panel physicians to find an authorized doctor — you cannot use your family doctor unless they are on that list
A valid credit or debit card to pay the physician's fee
steps.cost: Paid directly to the panel physician; fees vary from one doctor to another
steps.time_estimate: One in-person appointment; book several weeks before your intended travel date so results reach the visa office in time

steps.title: Arrange your international transfer for Term 1 tuition (due September 9, 2026)
steps.why: Your Term 1 Winter Session tuition is due September 9, 2026 — it covers Term 1 courses, the first half of two-term courses, and most student fees. Once your fees are assessed you'll see the exact amount under "Finances" in Workday, and until then you can estimate with UBC's cost estimator. Because you're paying from abroad, start the transfer early: on a major, liquid currency corridor a standard bank wire or transfer service clears quickly, but you still need time for your bank's verification and for funds to post to your UBC account before the deadline. Budget for the other charges hitting your account around the same period too: the $3,000 acceptance deposit for students on a study permit (due between May 1 and June 1, per your letter of admission or the Applicant Service Centre), your first residence/meal plan instalment if you accepted a residence offer, the temporary iMED medical insurance fee of $237 ($338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee charged when you register for courses, and your second residence instalment on September 19, 2026.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer and paid the acceptance deposit through the Applicant Service Centre
Registered for courses so your fees are assessed
Checked your assessed fees under "Finances" in Workday
steps.cost: Term 1 tuition as assessed in Workday (use UBC's cost estimator beforehand), plus iMED $237 ($338 for one-term exchange students) + $10.54 direct billing fee, plus any residence/meal plan instalments
steps.time_estimate: 30-60 minutes to initiate; start 2-3 weeks before the September 9, 2026 deadline

steps.title: Prepare your port-of-entry documents and clear the border
steps.why: Your study permit approval isn't your study permit — if you applied from outside Canada, IRCC sends a port of entry letter of introduction and a border services officer issues the actual study permit when you arrive. The letter contains the permit reference number used to issue your permit, so arriving without it (or without the passport you applied with) can stop you from being issued the permit.
prerequisites: Approved study permit application with port of entry letter of introduction received in your IRCC online account
The same passport you used to apply for your study permit

Valid eTA (linked to that passport) or visitor visa in your passport, if you need one — or a valid green card/equivalent proof of U.S. status plus your national passport if you're a U.S. permanent resident
Copy of your valid UBC letter of acceptance (updated LOA if you deferred enrolment, with deferral approved by UBC)
Letters of reference or any other documents the visa office told you to bring
Proof of enough money for your stay
steps.time_estimate: Have documents in your carry-on before departure; border processing on arrival

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) with Service Canada
steps.why: A SIN is the 9-digit number you need to work in Canada, open most types of bank accounts, and access government programs and benefits — so you can't be paid for on-campus or off-campus work without one. As a temporary resident, your SIN starts with "9" and expires with your immigration documents, so you'll need to apply again to extend the expiry date when your study permit is renewed. Applying online gives faster processing, and Service Canada no longer issues plastic cards.
prerequisites: Be 12 years or older (anyone 12+ can apply for their own SIN)
One primary identity document proving your legal status in Canada (e.g. your study permit/immigration document)
One secondary identity document confirming your identity
Supporting documents if your name has changed, plus translations if a document is not in English or French

Check documents for errors before applying — contact the issuing source to fix any error first, and note that if your application details don't match your primary identity document, Service Canada records the name as it appears on that document
applies_to_rules: Temporary residents (study permit holders): SIN starts with "9" and expires with your immigration documents
You cannot edit a submitted application — if you make a mistake or forget a document, you must submit a brand-new application with all required documents again
If Service Canada cannot issue you a SIN, you may instead get a temporary tax number (TTN) from the CRA by attaching a letter explaining why to your tax or benefit application
If you already have a SIN and don't remember it, sign in to or register for My Service Canada Account (MSCA) to view and print it instead of reapplying

steps.title: Apply for BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) after you arrive, and rely on iMED in the meantime
steps.why: All B.C. residents must enrol in the Medical Services Plan, and if you don't have other medical coverage you are required by BC law to register for MSP. As someone new to Canada, you should apply as soon as you arrive — coverage may only start three months after your arrival date in British Columbia, so if you arrive in August your waiting period will likely end in November. UBC covers that gap for international students with temporary iMED medical insurance, which is charged to your account when you register for courses and covers you until your MSP coverage begins (likely in November). The BC government also advises getting private health care insurance while you wait. Note that coverage depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling for MSP, you may have to repay your medical expenses. Applying online is the easiest and fastest way to enrol; completing enrolment gets you your Personal Health Number (PHN). (Confirm with UBC which office administers MSP enrolment support for undergraduate students — that detail is not covered in the sources here.)
prerequisites: Arrive in British Columbia and establish residence (the 3-month wait period starts from your arrival date)
Be registered in courses at UBC, which triggers the iMED temporary insurance charge to your student account
Have your immigration/study permit documents on hand for the online MSP application
steps.cost: iMED: $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee. MSP premiums: $75/month for students on a study permit ($0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents).
steps.time_estimate: Apply as soon as you arrive; coverage may begin about three months after your arrival date in B.C. (November 1, 2026 onward if you arrived in August)

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month coverage wait period
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. New residents are only eligible after a wait period equal to the balance of the month in which residence is established, plus two months — so if you are new to Canada, coverage may not start until about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Confirming your application is progressing and bridging the gap with private insurance prevents you from facing uncapped medical bills during your first term.
prerequisites: MSP Application for Enrolment already submitted online, in person or by mail
Your B.C. arrival date (the wait period is calculated from the date residence is established)
ID documents used on your application, for reference when following up
If your coverage is through an employer, union or pension group plan, your group administrator's contact details
steps.cost: No application fee for MSP enrolment; budget separately for private health insurance to cover the wait period
steps.time_estimate: 30–45 minutes to follow up, plus ongoing until coverage starts (~3 months from arrival)
